source_text: Sed uobis dico, inquit, qui auditis — ostendens hoc olim mandatum a creatore: loquere in aures audientium —-.diligiteinimicosuestrosetbenediciteeos, qui uos oderunt, et orate pro eis, qui uos calumniantur. haec creator una pronuntiatione clusit per Esaiam: dicite 'fratres nostri estis' eis, qui uos oderunt. si enim qui inimici sunt et oderunt et maledicunt et calumniantur fratres appellandi sunt, utique et benedici odientes et orari pro calumniatoribus iussit qui eos fratres deputari praecepit. 'Nouam plane patientiam docet Christus, etiam uicem iniuriae cohibens permissam a creatore, oculum exigente pro oculo et dentem pro dente, contra ipse alteram amplius maxillam offerri iubens et super tunicam pallio quoque cedi.' plane. (ni) haec Christus adiecerit ut supplementa consentanea disciplinae creatoris. atque adeo hoc statim renuntiandum est:
pass_a_gloss: But to you I say, he says, who hear — showing this once commandment from the creator: speak in the ears of those hearing — love your enemies and bless those who hate you, and pray for those who calumniate you. The creator closed these with one utterance through Esaiam: say 'you are our brothers' to those who hate you. For if those who are enemies and hate and curse and calumniate are to be called brothers, certainly he also commanded to bless those who hate and to pray for calumniators, who ordered them to be considered brothers. Christ indeed teaches new patience, even restraining the revenge of injury permitted by the creator, demanding an eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth, but himself commanding to offer the other cheek and to give up the cloak besides the tunic. Indeed. If Christ added these as supplements consistent with the creator's discipline. And so this must be announced immediately:

choices.why: means by which the creator spoke

pass_b_english: He's speaking directly to those who are listening, and what he's saying is rooted in a command from the Creator. The message is clear: love your enemies, bless those who hate you, and pray for those who slander you. This isn't a new idea - the Creator made this point through the prophet Isaiah, who told us to look at our enemies as brothers. If we're supposed to consider them brothers, even when they're cursing us and spreading lies about us, then it logically follows that we should bless them and pray for them. Christ is teaching us about a new kind of patience, one that goes beyond just accepting the status quo. He's saying that even when we've been wronged, we shouldn't seek revenge, even though that's what the law allows - an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth. Instead, Christ tells us to offer the other cheek and to give up our cloak as well as our tunic. If Christ is adding to the Creator's teachings, then his message is one of radical forgiveness and love. This is a message that needs to be shared immediately.

review.notes: Pass B is a paraphrase/interpretation rather than a translation and fails to preserve the specific agency and structure of the Latin. Specifically, Pass B omits the direct quote structure 'Sed uobis dico, inquit' (But to you I say, he says) and replaces the specific clause 'Christus... etiam uicem iniuriae cohibens permissam a creatore' (Christ... even restraining the voice/revenge of injury permitted by the creator) with a generalized interpretation. Most critically, Pass B fails to translate the final sentence 'atque adeo hoc statim renuntiandum est' (And so this must be announced/renounced immediately) accurately, turning it into a moralizing conclusion 'This is a message that needs to be shared immediately' which changes the semantic force of the Latin 'renuntiandum est' (must be renounced/declared).
reasons: Pass B fails to maintain the formal structure and specific meaning of the Latin, particularly in the final sentence where 'atque adeo hoc statim renuntiandum est' is rendered as a moral exhortation 'This is a message that needs to be shared immediately' instead of the required translation of the passive periphrastic 'this must be renounced/declared immediately'.
